$comment: Runtime: src/jobs/screener.py (MATCHER_SYSTEM). Runs inside the search pipeline (services/search_service.run_search); not a chat agent.
name: job_matcher
description: Semantic screening: judges each shortlisted posting against the profile summary (realistic role families only) and the career intent, and returns a verdict.
model_role: screening (first pass); quality (second opinions on every match and near the threshold)
input: ProfileSummary (role families code rejected are removed), with the preferences the user accepted from their labels (services.learning)
posting digests (batch of 3, or 1 for a second opinion); long descriptions keep their requirements section (3000 chars)
output: JobAssessment {job_id, fit_summary, reasons, transferable, gaps, essential_unmet, unknowns, dealbreakers, alignment (against|neutral|aligned), alignment_note, ratings {function, domain, seniority, leadership, sector, practicality: level 0-4}} -> screener.finalize -> JobVerdict {+ dimensions (points: level/4 of weights 30/20/20/10/10/10), fit_score, band, priority, match, borderline, cap_reason, reviewed, from_memory}

batching.shortlist: every posting sharing a role word with the target roles + 10 best others (screen_extra), ceiling 250 (screen_max_jobs); 40 when there are no target roles
batching.shortlist_order: titles sharing a role-specific word with the target roles first, then pre-filter score; one per (employer, title)

decision: code: points = level/4 of each weight; fit_score = their sum, capped at 65 if an essential is unmet or a dimension < 40% of its weight; match = fit_score >= threshold (default 60) AND no dealbreakers; borderline = |fit_score - threshold| <= 5 and no dealbreakers; alignment never changes fit_score: 'against' caps priority at 'consider' and lowers the rank by 10 points

consistency.memory: data/verdict_cache.json keyed by normalized posting text (known company aliases and presentation-only description labels) + profile summary + career intent + constraints + provider:screening model:effort|review:quality model:effort + MATCHER_VERSION
consistency.second_opinion: every first-pass match, postings within 5 points of the threshold, or scoring 65-80 with seniority and leadership both at levels 2-3: one more single-posting assessment by the quality model, levels averaged and rounded down

sector_and_domain: profile-driven (the profile's domains), not tied to one industry; adjacent role families are rated on how much of the work their evidence covers, never a dealbreaker on discipline alone
